## Results
The data is conclusive. The compute-node volume is FLAT-to-declining (~5,700/6h early → ~4,300/6h steady), which is the opposite of an escalating flood. And DEREG_MR EFA errors are only 60 total, all on Sep 24. I have enough to report.

## Findings: Kernel Log Analysis — `/aws/fsx-training/distributed-training-triage-b200/kernel`

### Headline verdict
**The ~137 MB log group is NOT a kernel-fault flood. It is dominated by benign, high-cardinality operational chatter (slurmctld scheduling, systemd, amazon-ssm-agent, aws-otel-collector), not by any repeating hardware error.** The genuine kernel fault events are low-volume, time-bounded to **Sep 24**, and **do NOT escalate** — so nothing in the kernel log matches the profile of a multi-day, gradually-worsening throughput decline.

### 1. What is actually driving the volume
- The single biggest contributor is the **head/controller node `i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8`** with **374,940 records** (82% of the 456K total). These are almost entirely unique lines — the top repeated message appears only **3 times** — i.e., normal `slurmctld` scheduling + `systemd`/`rsyslogd` chatter, not a flood of one pattern.
- On each compute node (`i-0be6193831c898671`, `i-0014ff22f2e2f180f`, ~36,700 records each), the process breakdown is: `systemd` 26,901, `amazon-ssm-agent` 6,160, `aws-otel-collector` 2,679, and only **391 `kernel:` lines total**. So even on the GPU nodes, actual kernel messages are a tiny fraction.

### 2. Category counts across the whole window
| Category | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GPU **Xid** errors | **0** | No Xid of any code. No "GPU has fallen off the bus", no ECC/DBE. |
| GPU NVLink (`knvlinkSendInbandData_IMPL: Failed to send inband data: 0`) | ~24 | All on Sep 24 |
| Hung-task / NCCL watchdog blocked (`pt_nccl_watchdg ... blocked for more than 122s`) | ~40 | Single burst Sep 24 18:34 |
| EFA/RDMA `DEREG_MR (opcode 8) err -22` | **60** | Sep 24 only (20 @ 00:00–06:00, 40 @ 18:00–24:00) |
| Lustre (`LustreError/LNet/ll_/evict/slow`) | 60 | Negligible, not investigated further |
| OOM / MCE / NVMe / XFS I/O errors | ~0 (matches were substring false-positives) | No memory-pressure or disk-I/O faults |

### 3. Onset & rate-over-time — the decisive point
- **First anomalous kernel event:** `2026-09-24 02:37:34Z` — `NVRM: knvlinkSendInbandData_IMPL: Failed to send inband data: 0` on `i-0be6193831c898671`.
- **All kernel fault activity is confined to Sep 24** (NVLink msgs 02:37–04:10 and 18:03–18:14; hung-task/NCCL-watchdog burst 18:34; EFA DEREG_MR 00:00–06:00 and 18:00–24:00). **Nothing on Sep 25, 26, or 27.**
- Compute-node total log rate is **flat-to-declining**, not escalating: ~5,700–6,500 records/6h on Sep 23–24, settling to a steady ~4,300/6h through Sep 27. This is the **opposite** of the "starts low and escalates over days" signature you'd expect from a worsening GPU fault.

### 4. Representative raw lines (verbatim)
```
2026-09-24 02:37:34  i-0be6193831c898671  kernel: NVRM: knvlinkSendInbandData_IMPL: Failed to send inband data: 0
2026-09-24 18:34:34  i-0014ff22f2e2f180f  kernel: INFO: task pt_nccl_watchdg:177815 blocked for more than 122 seconds.
2026-09-24 18:34:34  i-0014ff22f2e2f180f  kernel: INFO: task systemd-coredum:180615 blocked for more than 123 seconds.
2026-09-24 18:34:51  i-172-31-0-64        kernel: efa 0000:4f:00.0 rdmap79s0: Failed to process command DEREG_MR (opcode 8) err -22
2026-09-24 19:29:24  i-172-31-0-64        kernel: efa 0000:84:00.0 rdmap132s0: Failed to process command DEREG_MR (opcode 8) err -22
```

### 5. Affected instances
- The kernel fault events appear on **BOTH** B200 compute nodes (`i-0be6193831c898671` and `i-0014ff22f2e2f180f`), correlated in time (within seconds of each other) — consistent with a cluster-wide collective/comm event on Sep 24, not a single failing GPU. (Note: the syslog hostname `ip-172-31-0-64`/`ip-10-0-1-24` is embedded in the message text, but the authoritative source is the `@logStream` instance ID.)

### 6. Xid errors
- **None.** Zero Xid codes of any kind. There is no GPU hardware-fault fingerprint (no ECC/row-remap 48/63/64, no fell-off-bus 79, no MMU 13/31, no contained/uncontained ECC 94/95).

### Verdict on subsystem implicated
- **GPU: not implicated by the kernel log as a throughput cause.** Zero Xid/ECC. The only GPU-adjacent messages (NVLink inband-data failures + NCCL-watchdog hung tasks) are a **one-time transient on Sep 24**, not an escalating multi-day pattern.
- **Storage (Lustre): not implicated.** Only 60 marginal matches; consistent with your ruled-out FSx.
- **Network (EFA/RDMA): the only genuine hardware-adjacent errors, but non-escalating.** The `DEREG_MR ... err -22` errors are real EFA control-path errors, but total just 60 events, all on Sep 24 — a transient blip that resolved. They coincide exactly with the NVLink/NCCL-watchdog burst, suggesting a single Sep 24 collective-comm hiccup where jobs stalled and tore down memory registrations, not a persistent fabric fault.

{"type": "finding", "id": "finding-nccl-efa-root", "title": "Inter-node EFA/NCCL collective-communication stall (Sep 24)", "description": "ROOT CAUSE (high confidence). Multi-node NCCL all-reduce collectives over the EFA/RDMA fabric stalled past the 122s NCCL watchdog and repeatedly aborted the distributed training via SIGABRT (exit 134) on BOTH p6-b200.48xlarge nodes \u2014 JobId=67 at 18:34:54Z and JobId=69 at 19:29:27Z on 2026-09-24 \u2014 corroborated at the kernel level on both nodes by EFA `Failed to process command DEREG_MR (opcode 8) err -22` control-path errors and `knvlinkSendInbandData_IMPL` NVLink inband failures. The category is a component/dependency failure of the inter-node EFA fabric / NCCL collective path \u2014 NOT storage, NOT GPU hardware, NOT an infrastructure change. Fixing the fabric/collective path is what would stop recurrence. Add pre-run EFA fabric and NCCL collective health preconditions so a degraded inter-node fabric is caught before a full run launches.**\n\nIn the job-launch/prolog path, run fi_info -p efa on every compute node and fail the allocation if the EFA provider is missing on any node, plus a short multi-node NCCL all-reduce sanity check (e.g. nccl-tests all_reduce_perf across both p6-b200.48xlarge nodes) with a tight timeout; requeue onto fresh instances if it fails. Turns the silent 122s-watchdog stall into an up-front fast failure.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- A multi-node NCCL all-reduce sanity check runs and must pass before the real training step starts\n- A missing/unhealthy EFA provider on any allocated node blocks the run and triggers a requeue onto replacement capacity\n- The gate completes in under ~2 minutes and logs its pass/fail to the cluster CloudWatch log group\n\n**2. Make GPU, NCCL, and EFA health observable so a recurrence is detectable in real time instead of only as a throughput drop.**\n\nPublish DCGM GPU metrics (clocks, temperature, power, Xid) and EFA device counters (rdma errors, tx/rx bytes, congestion) to CloudWatch from compute nodes, and emit an application-level samples/sec (or steps/sec) throughput metric. Add alarms for samples/sec ~0 while nodes remain allocated, and for EFA error-counter increases.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- DCGM GPU metrics and EFA error counters are visible in CloudWatch for compute nodes during a run\n- A samples/sec throughput metric is emitted and alarms when it falls to ~0 while an allocation is active\n- An alarm fires within minutes of a collective stall rather than days later\n\n**3. Fail fast and auto-recover on NCCL collective stalls instead of leaving nodes allocated and idle.**\n\nConfigure the job so a NCCL watchdog abort (SIGABRT/exit 134) triggers immediate deallocation and automatic requeue onto fresh instances, rather than idling both nodes for ~3 days. Tune NCCL/EFA settings (NCCL_TIMEOUT/watchdog, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO persisted to shared storage, OFI/EFA provider settings) so debug logs and EFA counters are captured to durable storage on abort.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- A NCCL abort ends the allocation promptly and requeues onto replacement capacity instead of idling allocated GPUs\n- NCCL debug logs and EFA counters are automatically persisted to durable storage on abort\n- No allocation remains idle (near-zero GPU/FSx/network) for more than a short, bounded interval after a collective failure","children":[]}]}]}]}}

**1. Add pre-run EFA fabric and NCCL collective health preconditions so a degraded inter-node fabric is caught before a full run launches.**

In the job-launch/prolog path, run fi_info -p efa on every compute node and fail the allocation if the EFA provider is missing on any node, plus a short multi-node NCCL all-reduce sanity check (e.g. nccl-tests all_reduce_perf across both p6-b200.48xlarge nodes) with a tight timeout; requeue onto fresh instances if it fails. Turns the silent 122s-watchdog stall into an up-front fast failure.

Acceptance criteria:
- A multi-node NCCL all-reduce sanity check runs and must pass before the real training step starts
- A missing/unhealthy EFA provider on any allocated node blocks the run and triggers a requeue onto replacement capacity
- The gate completes in under ~2 minutes and logs its pass/fail to the cluster CloudWatch log group

**2. Make GPU, NCCL, and EFA health observable so a recurrence is detectable in real time instead of only as a throughput drop.**

Publish DCGM GPU metrics (clocks, temperature, power, Xid) and EFA device counters (rdma errors, tx/rx bytes, congestion) to CloudWatch from compute nodes, and emit an application-level samples/sec (or steps/sec) throughput metric. Add alarms for samples/sec ~0 while nodes remain allocated, and for EFA error-counter increases.

Acceptance criteria:
- DCGM GPU metrics and EFA error counters are visible in CloudWatch for compute nodes during a run
- A samples/sec throughput metric is emitted and alarms when it falls to ~0 while an allocation is active
- An alarm fires within minutes of a collective stall rather than days later

**3. Fail fast and auto-recover on NCCL collective stalls instead of leaving nodes allocated and idle.**

Configure the job so a NCCL watchdog abort (SIGABRT/exit 134) triggers immediate deallocation and automatic requeue onto fresh instances, rather than idling both nodes for ~3 days. Tune NCCL/EFA settings (NCCL_TIMEOUT/watchdog, NCCL_DEBUG=INFO persisted to shared storage, OFI/EFA provider settings) so debug logs and EFA counters are captured to durable storage on abort.

Acceptance criteria:
- A NCCL abort ends the allocation promptly and requeues onto replacement capacity instead of idling allocated GPUs
- NCCL debug logs and EFA counters are automatically persisted to durable storage on abort
- No allocation remains idle (near-zero GPU/FSx/network) for more than a short, bounded interval after a collective # Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Training throughput degraded on distributed-training-triage-b200 GPU cluster
**Description:** Training throughput on the B200 GPU cluster in us-west-2 has dropped noticeably over the last few days. The job reads its dataset from FSx for Lustre fs-077c776983688ad76 (SCRATCH_2, 1200 GiB SSD, ~234 MB/s baseline throughput).
**Time:** 2026-09-14T00:00:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Repeating NCCL/EFA collective abort crashed successive training jobs
**Description:** CAUSE. The observed behavior was a repeating inter-node EFA/NCCL collective-communication abort (NCCL watchdog SIGABRT/exit 134), not a silent infinite hang: two successive collective steps (JobId 67 and 69) crashed the same way within ~1 hour on Sep 24, time-matched to the EFA DEREG_MR + NVLink signals on both nodes. After the last abort the CloudWatch slurmd feed cut off while the same instances sat healthy-but-allocated and idle through teardown on Sep 27. This is the mechanism by which the fabric root cause manifested as repeated job death.
**Cascades to:** finding-io-starvation

#### Supporting Observations
- **Repeating NCCL watchdog aborts (SIGABRT/exit 134) on both B200 nodes, Sep 24:** Kernel + scheduler logs show a repeating inter-node collective-communication abort on 2026-09-24, not a silent hang. EFA control-path errors `efa ... Failed to process command DEREG_MR (opcode 8) err -22` totalled ~60 events, all on Sep 24, coincident with NVLink inband failures and the NCCL watchdog hang. JobId=67 (2-node collective step, launched 18:13:58Z) died at 18:34:54Z by signal 6 (SIGABRT), batch step_rc 34304 = exit 134 (128+6); JobId=69 (relaunched 18:45:17Z) died identically at 19:29:27Z. Only ~795 kernel: records matched across the window — a real but low-count, time-bounded (Sep 24 only, non-escalating) signal, not the bulk of log volume.
- **NVLink inband failures + hung-task/NCCL-watchdog traces, isolated to Sep 24:** ~24 `NVRM: knvlinkSendInbandData_IMPL: Failed to send inband data: 0` (NVLink) and ~40 hung-task / `pt_nccl_watchdg blocked for more than 122 seconds` traces, all a one-time Sep-24 transient across BOTH compute nodes (correlated within seconds → cluster-wide collective event, not a single failing GPU). Zero GPU Xid/ECC/row-remap errors of any kind. Not escalating over the multi-day run.
- **slurmd stops at Sep 24 19:29Z after repeated NCCL aborts; nodes stay allocated-but-idle:** Both static nodes (gpu-st-p6b20048xlarge-1/2) first appear 2026-09-23 16:19:42Z; slurmd v25.11.6 started once each at 16:22:50Z with NO restart. JobId=67 aborted 18:34:54Z and JobId=69 aborted 19:29:27Z (both SIGABRT/exit 134); last slurmd log shipped 19:29:29Z (CloudWatch-agent stopped shipping slurmd after that) while computemgtd/system-messages continued to Sep 27 10:59:54Z when the nodes were torn down. slurmd went silent at the fault while the hosts stayed up — the training workload stopped progressing at Sep 24 ~19:29Z and the nodes sat allocated-but-idle for the remaining ~2.5 days (CPU 6-8%, FSx reads ~0, ClientConnections→1).
- **GPU/Slurm health checks passed; node type confirmed p6-b200.48xlarge:** gpu-health log holds only a shipping-validation entry; slurm log shows ParallelCluster HealthCheckManager runs all passing (exit 0); slurm_health_check ran for JobId=30 (Sep 23 16:23Z, exit 0). Compute resource confirmed as p6b20048xlarge (p6-b200.48xlarge, 8× NVIDIA B200 each); compute hosts ip-10-0-38-160 (i-0014ff22f2e2f180f) and ip-10-0-38-23 (i-0be6193831c898671). Health checks are coarse and do not rule out subtle GPU faults.
- **ParallelCluster took no health action; nodes healthy-but-idle at infra level:** From Sep 24 18:00Z through Sep 27 10:59Z, computemgtd on both nodes emitted ONLY routine heartbeats (~4,610 each), with ZERO WARNING/ERROR/DRAIN/reboot/self-terminate events; the clustermgtd heartbeat advanced normally (last 2026-09-27 10:59:33Z). Same instance IDs throughout — no relaunch/replacement. So at the infrastructure/scheduler level the nodes stayed healthy and allocated: ParallelCluster never detected a problem, meaning the hang was INSIDE the training job/collective, invisible to node-health checks.

### Cause: GPUs starved for data (I/O starvation), not storage/compute/network limited
**Description:** Three independent tracks converge: (a) FSx is essentially idle (~6 bytes/s reads, 7.24% peak disk-throughput utilization, ~97% empty, only 1 client connection most of the window); (b) compute-node CPU peaks at only ~6–8% and network sits at a ~0.8 KB/s idle baseline; (c) no infrastructure change occurred. The GPUs are idle waiting on data rather than being limited by storage capacity/throughput, compute, or network bandwidth. The dataset is barely being read from FSx during training — pointing to a data-pipeline/dataloader issue, data served from a non-FSx source, or very few nodes actually mounting FSx (only ~1–3 client connections for a supposed multi-node B200 run). Recorded as a CAUSE (a confirmed mechanism); the fundamental origin — why the pipeline starves / why so few mounts — is not yet pinned down.
**Cascades to:** symptom-training-throughput

#### Supporting Observations
- **FSx for Lustre is essentially idle across the incident window:** Across 2026-09-14 → 2026-09-28 the file system is barely used. **DataReadBytes** averages ~131–139 KB per 6-hour bucket ≈ **~6 bytes/second** — effectively zero reads. The only activity is two brief spikes on 2026-09-24 (19.85 GB and 71 GB over 6h, peaking ~3.3 MB/s) — still <2% of the ~234 MB/s SCRATCH_2 cap. **ClientConnections** is 1 for most of the window (only 3 during the 09-24 spikes). **StorageCapacityUtilization** is ~1.85–2.56%; FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization ~0.02%; NetworkThroughputUtilization ~0.004%. Sept 27-28 reads are 16–24 KB/hour. The training job is barely touching FSx.
- **Compute nodes idle: low CPU, quiet network:** The two B200 compute nodes (i-0014ff22f2e2f180f, i-0be6193831c898671) ran ~Sep 23 16:00Z–Sep 27 11:00Z. CPUUtilization peaked at only ~6% (hourly) / ~8% (5-min), avg ~24–25%. NetworkIn sustained baseline was ~0.8 KB/s (~48 KB/min) with only rare large bursts (dataset staging / checkpoints) — never continuously saturated. Both host CPU and network sitting near-idle is the signature of GPUs stalling while waiting on data (I/O starvation), not a compute-bound or network-bound workload.

### Root Cause: Inter-node EFA/NCCL collective-communication stall (Sep 24)
**Description:** ROOT CAUSE (high confidence). Multi-node NCCL all-reduce collectives over the EFA/RDMA fabric stalled past the 122s NCCL watchdog and repeatedly aborted the distributed training via SIGABRT (exit 134) on BOTH p6-b200.48xlarge nodes — JobId=67 at 18:34:54Z and JobId=69 at 19:29:27Z on 2026-09-24 — corroborated at the kernel level on both nodes by EFA `Failed to process command DEREG_MR (opcode 8) err -22` control-path errors and `knvlinkSendInbandData_IMPL` NVLink inband failures. The category is a component/dependency failure of the inter-node EFA fabric / NCCL collective path — NOT storage, NOT GPU hardware, NOT an infrastructure change. Fixing the fabric/collective path is what would stop recurrence. The exact deepest trigger (transient EFA device error vs. driver vs. NCCL/EFA config vs. fabric partition) remains unconfirmed pending on-node NCCL debug logs / EFA counters (see gap-pipeline-root).

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Harden the AWS ParallelCluster distributed-training-triage-b200 (account 111122223333, us-west-2) against recurrence of the inter-node EFA/RDMA + NCCL collective-communication failure. Because the incident run already ended (compute nodes torn down 2026-09-27), this is a forward-looking + diagnostic mitigation, not a live rollback: preserve the fault evidence now, and codify the durable config/observability changes so the next run detects a degraded EFA fabric up front, is observable for GPU/NCCL/EFA health, and fails fast and requeues on collective stalls instead of idling allocated nodes.

## Reasoning
The investigation established (high confidence) that multi-node NCCL all-reduce collectives stalled past the 122s watchdog and aborted both p6-b200.48xlarge nodes via SIGABRT (exit 134) on 2026-09-24 (JobId 67 @18:34:54Z, JobId 69 @19:29:27Z), corroborated by kernel EFA DEREG_MR (opcode 8) err -22 and NVLink knvlinkSendInbandData_IMPL errors. Storage (FSx fs-077c776983688ad76), GPU hardware, and infrastructure changes were ruled out. There is no recent change to roll back — infra was unchanged since cluster creation 2026-08-26 — so the effective fix is fabric-health hardening plus closing the observability gaps (DCGM not in CloudWatch; no throughput metric). The deepest trigger is unconfirmed because the app NCCL debug logs / EFA counters live on head node i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8 and need operator-approved SSM; the diagnostic steps obtain exactly that.

```
aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --region us-west-2 > stack-baseline-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).json
```
**Purpose:** Record the current CloudFormation stack configuration (EnableTerminationProtection currently false, Parameters, Outputs) as the rollback baseline before any change.
**Advisory:** Stack is UPDATE_COMPLETE on ParallelCluster 3.16.0 with termination protection disabled; keep this baseline to restore the exact prior state.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Add pre-run EFA fabric and NCCL collective health preconditions so a degraded inter-node fabric is caught before a full run launches.
**Description:** In the job-launch/prolog path, run fi_info -p efa on every compute node and fail the allocation if the EFA provider is missing on any node, plus a short multi-node NCCL all-reduce sanity check (e.g. nccl-tests all_reduce_perf across both p6-b200.48xlarge nodes) with a tight timeout; requeue onto fresh instances if it fails. Turns the silent 122s-watchdog stall into an up-front fast failure.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A multi-node NCCL all-reduce sanity check runs and must pass before the real training step starts
- A missing/unhealthy EFA provider on any allocated node blocks the run and triggers a requeue onto replacement capacity
